reviews.reason: OCCT reads a valid solid whose default BRepGProp volume is 2.0e-3 and area 8.2e-4 relative above 200 pi and 130 pi (its adaptive integration: within 6.5e-12). The kernel translates every entity but its validator refuses the body: the circles are rational quarter arcs with knots of multiplicity 2 (the degree) at the quarter points, and R4 certifies C1 of the homogeneous curve, which fails there (the rational curve is C1: its weights alone jump). The issues are exactly the four arc edges, the two caps' pcurves derived from them and the two wall surfaces (tests/step.rs, quarter_arc_rational_circles_are_not_c1). Importing such bodies needs a rational C1 test or edges and faces split at those knots; both are open.
reviews.independent_evidence: The homogeneous control points around the knot u = 1 are (5w, 5w, w), (0, 5, 1), (-5w, 5w, w) with w = sqrt(2)/2 rounded: removing one copy of the knot needs the middle point to be the mean of its neighbours, (0, 5w, w), which it is not; the rational end derivatives 2w (P2 - P1) and 2w (P3 - P2) are both (-10w, 0).
